Subject: Draft incident synthesis (for review before external readout)

Team —

I put together a short synthesis of the 2026-11-01 service degradation that affected a subset of private deployments (notably Greenline Health's VPC instance). High level:

- What happened: an edge routing config regression caused a subset of requests to be misrouted to an older model shard which lacked the updated KV cache population hooks. This led to elevated tail latency and retries between 01:07–01:42 UTC.
- Impact: ~47 minutes of elevated error rate for ~2% of Greenline traffic; several HTTV requests timed out leading to degraded user experience.
- Root cause: automated config rollout missed a canary gate due to a metric name mismatch in the rollout job.
- Mitigation: rolled back the rollout at 01:43 UTC and applied a hotfix to validate rollout metrics.
- Current state: system stable, additional validation checks added to rollout pipeline.

I attached a draft postmortem and an SLA impact worksheet for numbers (postmortem_draft.pdf, sla_impact_sheet.xlsx). Please review for technical accuracy before we share externally. Specific asks:

1) Marissa — please review the customer-facing language and confirm the items we can share publicly (we should avoid internal tooling details).
2) Hannah — can you validate the telemetry timestamps and confirm the 01:07–01:43 UTC window?
3) Vivek/Markus — need guidance on whether to include an initial credit offer in the first external readout or reserve that for a follow-up.

I kept the draft concise; comments inline on the doc are easiest.

Thanks,

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
